transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2025-09-30 16:00 PDT
- Duration: ~48 minutes
- Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Maya (Redwood SE), Jordan (Synterra CTO), Priya (Synterra Eng Lead), Liam (Synterra SRE)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be rough):
Synterra is evaluating Redwood for a mixed deployment: hosted for dev and small workloads, Dedicated for production low-latency endpoints, and potential Private (VPC) for regulated data. Key concerns are gateway/proxy architecture, LangChain/LlamaIndex SDK integration, rate-limiting/quotas across teams, and observability hooks into Datadog/Prometheus. They requested security docs and a cost spreadsheet and want an end-to-end benchmark.

Topics: integration patterns, SDKs, gateway/proxy, rate limits/quotas, observability, private deployment requirements, pilot scope

[00:00] Alex (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick go-round, who we have?
[00:05] Jordan (Synterra): Jordan here — CTO. We're scoped to pick a vendor for model serving and ways to integrate with our app layer.
[00:12] Priya (Synterra): Priya — engineering lead on the search team. We're the primary consumers, building a semantic overlay and vector search.
[00:18] Liam (Synterra): Liam, SRE. I'll be touching infra, quotas, and observability.
[00:22] Alex: Great. Maya from Redwood will cover technical patterns — SDKs, LangChain, LlamaIndex tie-ins, and the gateway options.
[00:29] Maya (Redwood SE): Hi, quick notes — Redwood offers Hosted API, Dedicated reserved pools, and Private (VPC / on-prem). We'll talk about how you might run a gateway/proxy in front for routing, rate-limits, and observability.

[02:05] Jordan: Our high-level ask — low latency for customer facing chat (P95 < 300ms ideally for short prompts), cost predictability, and data residency for some datasets. We currently have an internal gateway that fans requests to OpenAI and SageMaker endpoints based on model type.
[02:22] Maya: Ok, good context. On latency, Dedicated capacity can be pinned to provide consistent throughput and predictable latency SLOs. Hosted is more elastic but can vary; we have fallback routing to cheaper model variants.

[04:10] Priya: One big question — how does Redwood sit with LangChain and LlamaIndex? We use both in our ingestion and runtime pipelines.
[04:17] Maya: We have SDKs that are first-class — Python SDK aligns with LangChain callbacks and Retriever interfaces. For LlamaIndex, customers usually implement a small adapter; we can share example snippets. NOTE: sometimes the auto-transcription reads 'Llama index' as 'lama index' in docs, sorry.
[05:00] Alex: I'll share a repo link with the LangChain + Redwood SDK example.

[06:30] Liam: On quotas and rate limits — we operate multi-tenant teams with per-team budgets; we need per-route quotas and token-level tracking. Does Redwood expose token-level metering?
[06:41] Maya: Yes, we emit token and request metrics per-API key and per-model; Console shows token breakdown. For Dedicated you can also enforce per-route quotas at the edge (we support route config that maps to capacity pools). Caveat: if you run a customer-managed gateway you can enforce additional rate-limits there.

[08:50] Jordan: About the gateway/proxy — we've been debating building an extra proxy that shards by tenant and applies transform (e.g., prompt prep). We worry about KV cache invalidation if we have multiple frontends. How do you recommend?
[09:05] Maya: Two patterns: 1) Redwood as the primary endpoint and run a thin gateway in front for routing and transforms; leverage our prefix/KV cache so the heavy cache is close to runtime. 2) Put your gateway as ingress, and route to multiple Redwood model variants (hosted/dedicated/private). If you run external gateway you lose some of Redwood's automatic prefix caching unless you propagate cache keys.
[09:40] Priya: Is KV cache talk spelled out in docs? Our old notes say 'K V cash' sometimes in speech transcripts so wanted to confirm.
[09:47] Maya: Yes, it's KV cache — we can share the caching docs and examples for common prompt patterns.

[11:20] Jordan: Security — we need SAML SSO for console access, audit logs for model calls, and KMS integration for keys. Also SOC2 and ISO are mandatory.
[11:33] Alex: Redwood supports SSO (SAML/OIDC), RBAC, audit logs, and KMS integrations (customer-managed keys in Private). We have SOC 2 Type II; I'll attach the report.
[12:10] Priya: For Private deployment — is the control plane still Redwood-managed? Can we run the control plane in our VPC?
[12:20] Maya: We offer two Private patterns: (A) control plane in Redwood but with a customer network overlay and VPC peering, or (B) fully air-gapped on-prem package where control plane is customer-managed. Both support KMS/HSM. We'll send the architecture diagrams.

[14:45] Liam: Observability — we need traces, token-level timing, and hooks into Datadog and Prometheus. Is there a webhook or exporter?
[14:56] Maya: We push metrics to Prometheus-compatible endpoint for Dedicated and Private; Hosted has built-in dashboards and can forward metrics to Datadog. We also provide request-level traces you can export; many customers use our tracing hooks plus external APM. There are sample Grafana panels.

[17:10] Jordan: About model routing and fallbacks — can we policy-route by latency target and cost? Example: route low-latency traffic to Dedicated, and fall back to Hosted if Dedicated saturates.
[17:26] Maya: Yes, smart routing policies support tiered routing by capacity and latency SLOs. You can set canary policies and automatic fallback to a compatible model variant. We also support traffic split A/B rollouts.

[19:00] Priya: We use persistent KV cache across sessions to accelerate retrieval-augmented generation. Any gotchas for cache warming when moving from demo to prod?
[19:14] Maya: Cache warm-up is a common issue — suggest synthetic warm-up runs and traffic mirroring during rollouts. We can help design a rollout that pre-warms KV entries.

[21:35] Liam: Rate-limits again — we need hierarchical quotas: org-level, team-level, route-level. Can Redwood enforce hierarchical billing/quotas?
[21:47] Alex: The Console supports org-level quotas and per-route quotas; Dedicated has reserved capacity with quota enforcement; for more advanced hierarchies you can run a gateway in front and apply custom logic. We'll share a recommended configuration doc.

[23:50] Jordan: Integration with vector DBs — we plan to use Pinecone for nearest neighbor and then call Redwood for generation. Any recommended flow?
[24:05] Maya: Common flow: vector lookup -> top-k context -> prompt assembly -> generative call. We have a LangChain pipeline example where the Retriever calls Pinecone and the SDK sends the final prompt. Works well with low-latency Dedicated endpoints.

[26:30] Priya: If we embed an outbound gateway for attribution/logging, how redwood's SDK handle streaming responses and function/tool calling? We do a lot of streaming UIs.
[26:46] Maya: Our SDK supports streaming with chunked responses and tool-calling patterns. If you run a gateway, ensure it proxies chunked transfer encoding properly; otherwise the streaming experience can stall. We have a few gotchas documented for Nginx/proxy defaults.

[29:00] Priya: Any limits on concurrent sessions per model on Dedicated? We have ~200 concurrent UI sessions at peak.
[29:09] Maya: Dedicated size depends on GPU and reserved tokens/sec. We'll map your concurrency + token per request to recommended pool sizes. Example: a single A10-based pool X supports ~Y concurrent short-turn sessions — we'll provide a sizing spreadsheet.

[31:20] Jordan: Audit trail for model outputs — can we keep per-request payloads for compliance? We might need 90 days for the compliance team.
[31:30] Alex: You can enable request logging; in Hosted logs are retained per plan and we can export to your S3 for longer-term retention for Dedicated/Private. For Private you control retention policies.

[33:50] Liam: Network topologies — if we go private VPC peering, what's egress behavior and routing? Any NAT or firewall requirements?
[34:00] Maya: We'll share a VPC peering guide. Typically route tables and security groups need to allow outbound to Redwood's inference subnets; if using a fully air-gapped on-prem deployment, there are different steps. We'll include sample security group rules.

[36:10] Priya: Can we run canaries between Hosted and Dedicated to validate model parity?
[36:18] Maya: Yes, you can run shadow traffic and compare outputs; Console has eval tooling to diff responses and we support per-prompt eval hooks. We'll propose a canary plan in the pilot scope.

[38:50] Jordan: Pricing — send expected TCO for a mixed Hosted + Dedicated pattern. We do monthly commitments for Dedicated.
[38:58] Alex: I'll share a cost model spreadsheet that includes token rates, reserved capacity pricing, and a sample burst/overage plan.

[40:30] Priya: Do you have a sample pilot contract or MSA for Dedicated?
[40:36] Alex: Yes, we have a pilot template and MSA. I'll loop in legal on the next email.

[42:05] Liam: Observability detail — what tags/labels do metrics carry? We'd like org_id, team_id, route, model_version.
[42:16] Maya: Metrics include api_key, model, model_version, route, latency_ms, tokens_in, tokens_out. You can add metadata in the request header for propagation.

[44:00] Jordan: A couple of small notes — we'd like to test edge-proxying to reduce RTT from our EU clients. Is Redwood multi-region?
[44:10] Maya: Yes, multi-region. Hosted supports regional endpoints; Dedicated can be provisioned in specific regions. For EU edge we'd recommend dedicated or a local proxy + hosted fallback.

[45:50] Alex: Quick recap and next steps: I'll share pricing spreadsheet and pilot template; Maya will send security pack and LangChain/LlamaIndex examples; Jordan will send sample traffic and token distribution; Liam will share contact list for SRE. We'll schedule a benchmark week of Oct 13th.
[46:10] Priya: Sounds good.
[46:20] Jordan: Thanks, talk soon.
[46:26] Alex: Thanks everyone.

End transcript.

Notes about transcription: there are a few minor mis-hearings — e.g., 'K V cash' instead of KV cache, and speaker labels may not align perfectly in auto-export. Intent preserved.
